title: CTF: IAM Policy Audit & Principle of Least Privilege Enforcement

theory.intro: CTF: IAM Policy Audit & Principle of Least Privilege Enforcement is a core security discipline in AWS cloud operations.

sections.heading: Understanding CTF: IAM Policy Audit & Principle of Least Privilege Enforcement
sections.content: In modern cloud environments, proper configuration of CTF: IAM Policy Audit & Principle of Least Privilege Enforcement ensures privilege boundaries and access controls prevent unauthorized resource manipulation.

sections.heading: Security Risks & Attack Vectors
sections.content: Misconfigurations related to CTF: IAM Policy Audit & Principle of Least Privilege Enforcement allow attackers to perform unauthorized reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and persistent access within your cloud tenant.

sections.heading: Defense & Mitigation Strategies
sections.content: Enforce strict principle of least privilege, continuous auditing via CloudTrail/Config, and automated guardrails.

key_terms.definition: Granting only minimum permissions required to perform job functions.
AWS auditing service tracking API activity across account resources.
Capturing and analyzing event logs for incident detection and forensics.

question.text: Which security framework principle best prevents cloud misconfigurations?
question.explanation: The Principle of Least Privilege ensures identities are restricted to minimum required permissions.
